title: Chest CT
what: A CT scan shows your lungs in thin slices, in much more detail than a regular x-ray. Usually no needle is needed.
why: For pneumonia, a long-lasting cough, if something was found on an x-ray, and for early lung cancer screening in smokers.
duration: usually 5 to 10 minutes in the room; the scan itself takes a few seconds
tell_doctor: If you are or could be pregnant
If your CT is with contrast: any allergy to iodine or contrast, and any kidney disease
If it is hard for you to hold your breath or lie with your arms up

prepare.title: Without contrast
prepare.text: No prep needed. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: With contrast
prepare.text: You are usually asked not to eat for 3 to 4 hours. Water is fine. Sometimes you need a creatinine blood test. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Metal
prepare.text: Take off necklaces, pendants, and underwire bras. Clothes with no metal on the chest are best.

bring: Past chest x-rays and CT scans, to compare
Your creatinine test result, if you were asked
steps: You lie on your back with your arms raised above your head
The table moves through a wide ring
When told, breathe in and hold your breath for a few seconds
If you have contrast, it goes into a vein and more pictures are taken
feel: It does not hurt. The machine makes noise
With contrast: a warm feeling and a metal taste. It passes in a minute
after: You can go back to your day straight away
After contrast, drink more water, unless your doctor said otherwise
The report is usually ready in a few hours or 1 to 2 days
red_flags: If breathing is very hard or your lips turn blue, do not wait for your appointment. Call emergency services
After contrast: itching, a rash, a swollen face, or trouble breathing. Tell the staff or call emergency services

faq.q: Why is a chest CT better than an x-ray?
faq.a: A CT shows the lungs in slices and can find small spots that an x-ray misses.

faq.q: What is a low-dose lung CT?
faq.a: It is a CT with a lower dose, used to check smokers for lung cancer. Your doctor orders it based on your age and how long you have smoked.
